description: Non-modal popup anchored to a trigger. PopoverTrigger is a real <button> with aria-haspopup="dialog" and aria-expanded; PopoverContent renders as role="dialog" in a portal and is keyboard-focusable (unlike HoverCard). Unlike Dialog, it does not darken the page and does not prevent interaction with elements outside.

keyboard.action: Opens the popover when the trigger is focused.
Moves focus through the popover's focusable contents.
Moves focus backwards within the popover.
Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger.

focus.notes: Focus is moved into the popover on open (first focusable element) and restored to the trigger on close. Focus is NOT trapped; Tab at the end of the popover moves to the next tabbable element on the page, which also dismisses the popover.

announcements: Trigger announces as a button with the "dialog" popup affordance and its expanded state.
Popover content is read as a dialog; consumers should provide an aria-label / aria-labelledby for the dialog if it contains a form or meaningful section.
screenReader.notes: Because Popover is non-modal, screen reader users may not realize the popover is open if they swipe past the trigger. Pair with a visible label or title so the relationship is obvious.

contrast.text: Content uses foreground over bg-popover; meets WCAG AA on the default theme
contrast.ui: Edge is a decorative ring-1 ring-foreground/10 hairline plus shadow-md; the trigger carries the interactive affordance

motion.reducedMotion: Uses data-open:animate-in with fade + zoom + slide utilities. Gate with motion-reduce:animate-none if strict compliance matters.

consumerResponsibilities: Provide an accessible name for the popover content when it's a distinct section (form, date picker). Use aria-label on PopoverContent or wrap its first child in a heading; PopoverTitle is a plain <div> and is not wired to aria-labelledby.
Use Popover for UI that should remain clickable alongside the rest of the page; use Dialog for interruptions that demand the user's attention.
Consider where initial focus should land. Radix focuses the first tabbable child by default, which may not be ideal (e.g. an "X" close button); use ref-based focus for precision.
